chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade mixing milk with water for the purpose of selling.

key_terms.لِلْبَيْعِ: For selling / for the purpose of trade
key_terms.يُشَابَ: To be mixed / diluted (passive form indicating the act of adulteration)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on mixing water with milk for sale?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Prophet’s (SAW) prohibition against adulterating milk with water for sale, a specific instance of *ghish* (deception) in trade. It reflects the broader Shia legal emphasis on transparency in commodity quality, where altering the natural state of goods to mislead buyers constitutes a violation of commercial justice. The ruling serves as a practical application of the general principle that honesty is a prerequisite for valid transactions in Islamic jurisprudence.
